title: Detection of native bounded constructibility by underlying coefficient modules
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0$, an algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k_0)$, and $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Let $T_0$ be separated of finite type over $k_0$ and put $T=T_0\times_{k_0}k$. Use $B_T$, the native module-object category $\mathcal A_T$, its geometric Frobenius fixed-pair category $\mathcal W_T$, and $\mathrm{WC}^{\mathrm{der}}(T_0)$ from [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework]. Let $R_T=p_T^*\underline\Omega$ for the finite-subextension-valued condensed coefficient [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Let $E_T:\mathcal A_T\simeq\mathcal M_T$ be the exact equivalence to internal $R_T$-modules in abelian sheaves [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] specified by sectionwise action transport along $\theta_T:R_T\cong B_T$ [lem-sf-locally-finite-coefficient-ring-realization, lem-sf-native-encoding-derived-operations]. Write $U_T:\mathcal W_T\to\mathcal A_T$ for forgetting Frobenius, and $V_T=D(E_T)D(U_T)$ on ordinary derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

A native module $M$ is constructible (Zariski locally admitting a finite locally closed constructible stratification with pro-etale locally finite free restrictions over $B$) if and only if $E_TM$ is constructible in the coefficient-module sense [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. In this setting the native local stratifications can be replaced by one finite stratification of all of $T$. A finite-dimensional constant scalar model $P$ of dimension $r$ corresponds to $R_U\otimes_\Omega P\cong R_U^{\oplus r}$ on a covering member $U$; rank zero and ranks varying between covering members are allowed.

For every $C\in D(\mathcal W_T)$ and every integer $n$ there is a natural cohomology identification
$$H^n(V_TC)\cong E_TU_TH^n(C),\qquad H^n(C)=0\ \Longleftrightarrow\ H^n(V_TC)=0.$$
Consequently $V_T$ preserves and reflects support in every cohomological interval $[a,b]$, and
$$C\in\mathrm{WC}^{\mathrm{der}}(T_0)\ \Longleftrightarrow\ V_TC\in D^b_c(T,\Omega)\ \Longleftrightarrow\ V_TC\in D_{ctf}(T,\Omega).$$
Here $D^b_c$ means bounded cohomology with constructible coefficient-module cohomology, and $D_{ctf}$ adds finite Tor amplitude [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible, det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude]. If $V_TC$ has cohomology in $[a,b]$ and constructible cohomology, its Tor amplitude is contained in $[a-1,b]$. These assertions compare predicates after forgetting; they assert no equivalence with fixed pairs in a derived category.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change] to the structure morphism of $T_0$ and $\operatorname{Spec}k\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$. Thus $T$ is separated of finite type over $k$. Since $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is affine, [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine] makes $T$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated. These are the hypotheses required for the global-stratification and Tor-amplitude tools below.

source.place: Base change of separated finite-type morphisms; qcqs over an affine base (the statements of the two cited nodes).

proof.text: For a covering member $U$ and a scalar space $P$ of dimension $r$, choose a basis $e_1,\ldots,e_r$. The maps $R_U\otimes_\Omega P\to R_U^{\oplus r}$, $s\otimes\sum_j c_je_j\mapsto(c_js)_j$, and $(s_j)_j\mapsto\sum_j s_j\otimes e_j$ are inverse $R_U$-linear maps: the balancing identity moves each $c_j$ between the two factors. These formulas hold on sections and commute with restriction, hence define the asserted sheaf isomorphism. For $r=0$ both maps are the unique maps between zero modules. By [lem-sf-native-encoding-derived-operations], $E$ is sectionwise action transport along $\theta$ and preserves restrictions; it therefore takes $B_U^{\oplus r}$ to $R_U^{\oplus r}$. No rank is required to be constant between different covering members.

source.place: Definition 6.8.3; explicit basis calculation under the sectionwise action encoding.

proof.text: The same encoding is used in [lem-sf-weil-verdier-module-constructibility-comparison]: it commutes with restriction to locally closed strata and identifies finite constant scalar models with native finite free models, using the same stratification and covering. Thus on any Zariski open carrying a native finite stratification, $E_TM$ has a coefficient finite stratification, and conversely. Apply [lem-sfb-constructible-zariski-locality] on the qcqs scheme $T$ of step 1: these local coefficient stratifications give one finite coefficient stratification of $T$. Transfer each stratum and its covering back by the inverse encoding to obtain a global native stratification. Conversely a coefficient constructible module already has a global finite stratification by [sk-def-sfb-constructible], and transferring it gives a native constructible module. This proves both the sheaf criterion and the global-stratification assertion; the argument also works for the empty scheme.

source.place: Definitions 6.8.3 and 6.8.6; Zariski-local-to-global refinement is the cited coefficient-locality tool (cf. Stacks 095E, lemma-constructible-quasi-compact-quasi-separated).

proof.text: By [lem-sf-native-weil-constructible-abelian], forgetting Frobenius $U_T$ is exact and conservative on the ambient abelian categories. By [lem-sf-native-encoding-derived-operations], $E_T$ is an exact equivalence. Apply [lem-pur-exact-derived-cohomology-coherence] first to $U_T$, then to $E_T$. Inverting its comparisons and composing gives $H^n(D(E_T)D(U_T)C)\cong E_TH^n(D(U_T)C)\cong E_TU_TH^n(C)$. The cited coherence statement makes this identification natural for every morphism in the ordinary unbounded derived category; no boundedness or replacement of this category by derived fixed pairs is used.

source.place: Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor; canonical cohomology comparison and composition as stated by lem-pur-exact-derived-cohomology-coherence.

proof.text: Exact functors preserve zero objects, so $H^n(C)=0$ implies $E_TU_TH^n(C)=0$. Conversely suppose the latter is zero. An equivalence reflects zero, so $U_TH^n(C)=0$. Since $U_T$ is conservative, the unique arrow $0\to H^n(C)$ is invertible: its image is the isomorphism $0\to0$. Hence $H^n(C)=0$. Together with step 4 this proves vanishing detection degree by degree, and therefore preservation and reflection of support in every interval $[a,b]$, by checking each integer outside the interval.

source.place: Tag 015F; zero detection from conservativity, with the explicit zero-object argument.

proof.text: By [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework], $C$ belongs to $\mathrm{WC}^{\mathrm{der}}(T_0)$ exactly when its cohomology is zero outside a finite interval and each $U_TH^n(C)$ is native constructible. Step 5 identifies the first condition with boundedness of $V_TC$. Steps 3 and 4 identify the second with constructibility of each $H^n(V_TC)$ in the finite constant scalar model sense of [det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude](1)-(2). That node defines precisely the coefficient $D^b_c$ used here. Thus the first equivalence follows in both directions, using the same cohomological interval.

source.place: Definitions 6.8.6 and 6.8.8; direct assembly of steps 3-5 with the two predicates.

proof.text: Apply [det-def-localizing-closure-ctf-equals-bc](2) with $X=T$ and $\Lambda=\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Its qcqs hypothesis is step 1, and $\Omega$ is one of its specified coefficient rings, with exactly the finite-subextension condensed convention fixed in the statement. If $V_TC$ is bounded constructible with cohomology in $[a,b]$, that clause gives Tor amplitude in $[a-1,b]$. Hence it lies in $D_{ctf}$. Conversely membership in $D_{ctf}$ includes bounded constructible cohomology by [det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude](4). This proves the second equivalence and the stated bound. Rank zero and the zero complex satisfy it as well; no hypothesis on the Frobenius action enters this step.

source.place: Clause (2), specialized to the algebraically closed coefficient field.
